title: Repo Scouting Log Entry
description: Shape of a single line in .context/repo-scouting/log.jsonl -- one JSON object per line (JSONL, not a JSON array). Enforced by scripts/validate-repo-scouting-log.sh; illustrated by assets/templates/repo-scouting-entry.yaml. Records that an external repo was investigated for techniques street-view-movie-maker could learn from or port, and what was decided -- not a decision registry (see SKILL.md).

url.description: The repo's GitHub URL, no trailing path beyond owner/repo. Duplicate-checked case-insensitively by the validation script -- GitHub URLs aren't case-sensitive in practice.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the date the repo was investigated.

repo_name.description: Short slug, e.g. 'sk-zk/streetlevel' -- owner/repo, not a full URL.

summary.description: One line: what the repo actually is. Not what it might be used for -- see reasoning for that.

verdict.description: NOTHING_NEW: different domain, or a strict subset of prior art already on file. INFORMS_EXISTING: added a note/section to an already-open finding or known-issue. NEW_FINDING_NEEDED: novel enough to warrant its own new .context/ file. PORT_CANDIDATE: a stronger signal, actually recommended for implementation. This records that a signal was raised, not the decision itself -- NEW_FINDING_NEEDED/PORT_CANDIDATE entries still get a separate finding or plan if acted on.

reasoning.description: Free text: why that verdict. Self-contained -- a reader with no other context should understand it without re-reading a chat transcript.

related.description: Optional list of relative .context/ file paths this investigation updated or spawned. Omit entirely if none. Checked for existence by the validation script, but only as a warning -- a path can legitimately point at a finding/plan not yet written.
